flags.name: REUSE
flags.says: A re-run keeps the links of the sources it reads again, in order.

flags.name: LITERAL
flags.says: Graph lists of one or two are written as literals.

flags.name: MICRO
flags.says: A manual `flush` leaves a queued microtask in place rather than queueing another.

flags.name: POP
flags.says: Unlinking from the end of a list pops, and a full unlink doesn't touch the old list.

flags.name: OWNKEYS
flags.says: Keyed writes compare the object's keys when there are far more readers than keys.

flags.name: ENDS
flags.says: `For` finds rows that stayed at either end by position, with no Map.

flags.name: SWAP
flags.says: Two rows or nodes that traded places cost two moves, and no longest-run search.

flags.name: ROWBOX
flags.says: A row is its item's box, not a row and a box.

flags.name: DEFER
flags.says: Rows are checked for repeated keys when a later pass could keep them, not as they're made.

flags.name: FLAT
flags.says: Rows of one element reach `place` as they are, not through `resolve`.

flags.name: TEXT
flags.says: A hole that's its parent's only child writes `textContent`.

flags.name: WIPE
flags.says: Emptying a parent the hole fills is one `textContent` write.

flags.name: SCAN
flags.says: A pass that moves nothing already placed doesn't look for what was.

flags.name: LINEAR
flags.says: Up to 8 rows between the ends are matched by scanning, with no Map to build.

flags.name: KEYREAD
flags.says: A row's key is read once as the row is made, not through its item in every binding (crates/weft-compiler, `hoist_key`).

flags.name: EVENT
flags.says: A delegated handler that's a function is one property write, not two calls (crates/weft-compiler).

flags.name: STEADY
flags.says: A hole that holds one text node writes a new primitive straight to it: no `place`, no reads from the DOM.

flags.name: ORDERED
flags.says: A flush whose effects were queued in creation order doesn't sort them.

flags.name: RECORD
flags.says: A hole's parent, marker and nodes are a plain record its one shared writer reads, not a closure per hole.

flags.name: INLINE
flags.says: The first reader of a source and the first source of a reader sit on the object itself, so one link is no array.

flags.name: CHAIN
flags.says: What an owner owns is a chain through the computations, so owning is no array.
